memo:
I'll start by researching the most relevant names before committing capital.
Critical finding: NVDA reports earnings today after the close. Let me check the broader tape and a few other names.
# Research Memo — Cycle 1

**Account:** 1,000 CHF managed budget, 100% cash, no legacy positions. Clean slate, no rebalancing obligations.

## Market Read

The single most important fact this cycle is one of timing, not valuation: **Nvidia reports tonight, after the US close.** 
Nvidia will report after the US close at around 22:00 CET, and while the past quarter is expected to be enormous, what will move markets is what CEO Jensen Huang says about the months ahead — the company has become a proxy for the entire AI rally, so if its outlook disappoints, the shockwaves will not stay in Silicon Valley.
 
Analysts expect adjusted earnings of $2.09 a share on revenue of roughly $92 billion, growth of 96% year-on-year.


Expectations are already elevated going in. 
Citi expects Nvidia to report $93 billion in revenue for the July quarter, about $1 billion above Wall Street consensus, helped by a continued strong ramp of its B300 chips, and expects revenue to rise another 13% sequentially to $105 billion in the October quarter.
 
The market expects Nvidia to forecast FY27Q3 revenue of $104 billion.
 When the sell side is already modelling *above* consensus, the bar for a positive surprise is high and the payoff is asymmetric to the downside.

Buying AI-beta with a $1,000 book eight hours before a binary event with a two-sided 6–10% distribution is not investing, it's a coin flip. The correct move is to build a core that does not need Nvidia's guide to work, and hold meaningful dry powder to buy the reaction rather than predict it.

**Sizing constraint worth naming:** with share prices this high, granularity is a real risk input. One SPY is 77% of the book, one QQQ is 71%, one AMD is 48%. Any single-share ETF purchase would make this a one-decision portfolio and — in QQQ's case — a heavily Nvidia-weighted one. That rules the index sleeve out at this budget.

## Positions to Open

**GOOGL — Buy 1 share, ~$342 (34% of budget).** The one megacap with a genuinely differentiated compute stack, so its AI story is less hostage to the Nvidia supply-and-guide narrative than any peer's. Headline flow is noise: 
an Ohio congressman sold up to $100K of Alphabet stock
 — irrelevant to the thesis.

**AMZN — Buy 1 share, ~$259 (26% of budget).** The cheapest entry on the list gives the book its best sizing granularity, and AWS plus retail margin gives two independent earnings drivers rather than one AI beta. 
Ring is adopting new measures to ensure the company cannot access clients' videos once processed
 — a modest privacy-overhang reducer, not the reason to own it.

**Total deployed: $600.19 (60%). Cash reserve: $399.81 (40%).**

## Passing This Cycle — and Why

**NVDA — no position.** I have no edge on tonight's print, and consensus is already braced for a beat. I would rather pay up tomorrow with information than guess tonight without it.

**AMD — pass, despite genuinely good news.** 
Raymond James upgraded AMD to Strong Buy from Outperform
, 
raising its price target to $641, with the company reporting record Q2 revenue of $11.5 billion, up 50% year-over-year
. But AMD trades as a high-beta Nvidia derivative: 
its stock has previously declined amid broader semiconductor sell-offs with investors cautious ahead of Nvidia's earnings
. At $483, one share is half the book strapped to someone else's earnings call. Right thesis, wrong hour, wrong size.

**META — pass on legal overhang.** 
A California trial has 29 state attorneys general accusing the company of illegally collecting children's data and misleading consumers about safety, with Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers set to decide the case alongside a nonbinding advisory jury verdict.
 
Meta was ordered to pay $567 million into an abatement fund after an earlier $375 million judgment in New Mexico, and the California case could have considerably broader consequences.
 The watchlist headline that a judge suspended a Meta trial and is inclined to approve a deal is a separate matter and, at $577 for one share, not enough to justify 58% of the book on an unresolved legal tree.

**AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, SPY, QQQ — pass.** No specific catalyst or edge; at these share prices each would crowd out diversification for no compensating thesis.

## Recommendation

**BUY 1 GOOGL (~$342) and 1 AMZN (~$259). Hold ~$400 cash.**

Deploy 60% into two megacaps whose theses survive any Nvidia outcome, and deliberately retain 40% dry powder into a known binary event. Next cycle, with the guide in hand, that reserve gets put to work — most likely into AMD on a washout, where the upgrade thesis is already validated and only the entry price is in question. If instead the guide is strong and semis gap up, I forgo that trade and add to quality on the next pullback rather than chase. No trade is a position, and this cycle 40% cash is an active one.

audit.summary:
This memo is the opposite of a black box. The manager named the single biggest risk in the tape (Nvidia reporting tonight), explained why they refuse to gamble on it, and sized accordingly. Both orders trace directly back to written theses: GOOGL for its in-house compute stack (less dependent on Nvidia's guide), AMZN for two separate earnings drivers plus the best share-price granularity at a 1,000 CHF budget. The manager also explicitly declined the names that would have been pure hype chases (NVDA into the print, AMD as a high-beta NVDA derivative, META with an unresolved legal tree) and gave concrete reasons for each pass. Nothing here contradicts its own stated risks.

Things worth your attention, not veto-worthy: the book is only two names, so 60% of deployed capital sits in two megacaps that will still correlate hard with any AI-wide drawdown — the 'survives any Nvidia outcome' claim is directionally true but overstated; GOOGL and AMZN will both take a hit if the AI trade unwinds. Also note the manager pre-committed to buying AMD on a washout next cycle; hold them to actually re-underwriting that at the time rather than treating it as a done deal, since a washout could mean the thesis broke, not that it went on sale. Finally, 40% cash is a defensible active choice here, but if it becomes a permanent habit it's just under-deployment — expect a plan next cycle.

Both orders approved.

order_reviews.reason: Directly and specifically supported by the memo: differentiated in-house compute stack means less exposure to the Nvidia supply/guide narrative, which is the memo's central risk. Size (34%) is stated, deliberate, and constrained by share-price granularity. Manager also correctly dismissed the congressman-sale headline as noise rather than dressing it up as a signal.

Clear, non-hype thesis: two independent earnings drivers (AWS and retail margin) rather than single-factor AI beta, and the lowest share price on the list gives the best sizing granularity at a 1,000 CHF budget. The Ring privacy headline is explicitly labelled as not the reason to own it, which is honest. Consistent with the memo's stated goal of a core that does not need Nvidia's guide to work.
